{{Short description|American neuroscientist}}
[[File:Vadim Bolshakov.jpg|thumb|Vadim Bolshakov in 2020]]

'''Vadim Bolshakov''' is a Russian-born American neuroscientist, a professor of psychiatry at [[Harvard Medical School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pinphd.hms.harvard.edu/people/vadim-bolshakov|title=Vadim Bolshakov|website=pinphd.hms.harvard.edu}}</ref> He has been Director of the Cellular Neurobiology Laboratory at [[McLean Hospital]] since 1999. He received The Esther A. and Joseph Klingenstein Fund award in 2001<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://klingenstein.org/esther-a-joseph-klingenstein-fund/|title=Esther A. & Joseph Klingenstein Fund|website=Klingenstein Philanthropies}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://klingenstein.org/grantees/grantee/ejk-neuroscience-fellows/2001/vadim-bolshakov-ph-d/|title=Vadim Bolshakov, Ph.D.|website=Klingenstein Philanthropies}}</ref> and NARSAD Distinguished Investigator award in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bbrfoundation.org/content/brain-behavior-research-foundation-awards-15-million-narsad-distinguished-investigator|title=The Brain & Behavior Research Foundation Awards $1.5 Million in NARSAD Distinguished Investigator Grants to Fund Cutting-Edge Research|date=November 7, 2013|website=The Brain & Behavior Research Foundation Awards $1.5 Million in NARSAD Distinguished Investigator Grants to Fund Cutting-Edge Research &#124; Brain & Behavior Research Foundation}}</ref> 

Bolshakov is an associate editor of ''Frontiers in Neural Circuits'', published by Frontiers,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neural-circuits/editors|title=Frontiers in Neural Circuits &#124; Editorial board|website=www.frontiersin.org}}</ref> an associate editor of ''[[Neurochemistry International]]'', published by Elsevier, and a consulting editor of ''Amino Acids'', published by Springer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/726/editorial-board|title=Amino Acids|website=SpringerLink}}</ref> He presently serves on the Scientific Council of the [[Brain & Behavior Research Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bbrfoundation.org/about/people/vadim-bolshakov-phd|title=Vadim Bolshakov, Ph.D.|date=October 7, 2021|website=Vadim Bolshakov, Ph.D. &#124; Brain & Behavior Research Foundation}}</ref>

In his work, he focuses on understanding the cellular and neural network-level mechanisms of learned and innate behaviors with an emphasis on studies of fear mechanisms in the brain. He demonstrated that negatively-charged memories, resulting in uncontrollable [[fear]] and [[anxiety]], are associated with long-term functional changes at synaptic contacts in the [[amygdala]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tsvetkov |first1=E. |last2=Carlezon |first2=W. A. |last3=Benes |first3=F. M. |last4=Kandel |first4=E. R. |last5=Bolshakov |first5=V. Y. |url=https://www.cell.com/neuron/fulltext/S0896-6273(02)00645-1|title=Fear Conditioning Occludes LTP-Induced Presynaptic Enhancement of Synaptic Transmission in the Cortical Pathway to the Lateral Amygdala: Neuron |journal=Neuron |date=2002 |volume=34 |issue=2 |pages=289–300 |doi=10.1016/s0896-6273(02)00645-1 |pmid=11970870 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2002/05/brain-changes-in-learning-measured/|title=Brain changes in learning measured|date=May 30, 2002|website=Harvard Gazette}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cho |first1=J. H. |last2=Deisseroth |first2=K. |last3=Bolshakov |first3=V. Y. |title=Synaptic Encoding of Fear Extinction in mPFC-amygdala Circuits: Neuron |journal=Neuron |date=2013 |volume=80 |issue=6 |pages=1491–1907 |doi=10.1016/j.neuron.2013.09.025 |pmid=24290204 |pmc=3872173 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsweek.com/mechanics-trauma-99053|title=The Mechanics of Trauma|author=Newsweek Staff|date=August 19, 2007|website=Newsweek}}</ref> He also demonstrated that these aversive memories, as well as synaptic modifications associated with them, can be controlled by the expression of specific genes in brain regions responsible for emotional states.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2005/12/researchers-find-a-gene-for-fear-2/|title=Researchers find a gene for fear|date=December 1, 2005|website=Harvard Gazette}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2005/11/23/mutant-mouse-gene-quells-fear-harvard/|title=Mutant Mouse Gene Quells Fear &#124; News &#124; The Harvard Crimson|website=www.thecrimson.com}}</ref> Overall, his findings provide evidence that [[synaptic plasticity]] in specific projections within behavior-controlling neural circuits may serve as a cellular mechanism of memory formation and retention.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Mechanisms of fear learning and extinction: synaptic plasticity–fear memory connection|first1=Natalia V.|last1=Luchkina|first2=Vadim Y.|last2=Bolshakov|date=January 1, 2019|journal=Psychopharmacology|volume=236|issue=1|pages=163–182|doi=10.1007/s00213-018-5104-4|pmid=30415278|pmc=6374177}}</ref>
